$comment: Boot-payload budget (#485 D), enforced by `node scripts/check-build-manifest.mjs --budget` in the 'Build without Emscripten' CI job and mirrored into vite.config.ts build.chunkSizeWarningLimit. Sizes are raw (un-gzipped) bytes of build/assets/*.js; 1 kB = 1000 bytes like Vite's reporter. Raise a number only with a reason in the PR; lower it whenever a phase earns the room.
entryNote: Ceiling = the entry after the follow-up split (698,257 B) rounded up to the next kB. Raised 699,000 -> 707,000 B (CI unbreak, Phase A): #508 (InputHub + KeyboardMouseSource, the ghost codec v4 input track) merged into the split's branch and put the entry at 707,769 B with every main run red; ScriptedSource (?input=script only) moved behind a dynamic import (-1.4 kB) and the rest is the hub every vehicle reads each frame, so it stays on the boot path: 706,350 B, rounded up. Raised 707,000 -> 709,000 B (#502, C ABI / worker-wire hardening): the main-thread wasm loader is on the boot path and gained the one-retry + fetch abort, the heap-exhausted error the bound allocateGrid throws, the HUD trap / heap rows and the cached segment sampler (+2.3 kB: 708,673 B); the trap parser itself was split out (wasmTrap chunk, loaded only for ?wasmTrapTest=1). The 700 kB target is missed by ~6 kB again. What left the entry, raw: Rapier glue + @react-three/rapier -> vendor-rapier (167 kB, statically imported so it is modulepreloaded and counted in bootJs); GLTFLoader (44 kB, first model preload), SSAOPass (12 kB, preset High) and SMAAPass (61 kB, aa tier smaa) behind composerPassModules, KTX2Loader + zstddec (60 kB, only fetched on a GPU with a compressed target); RaftVehicle (23 kB), WgslSweSim (22 kB, native WebGPU only); PauseMenu / SettingsPanel / RunResultsPanel and the physics / wireframe / SWE-bed overlays; LevelLoader and ReachManager + ReachStreamer + ReactiveAudio (?level= and ?reach= only); fauna, biome props and set pieces as one `extras` chunk (42 kB, preloaded at idle). Per-biome loading was NOT done per biome: the biome-exclusive decorations are ~38 kB pre-minify in total, so they share the chunk with the fauna instead of adding one request per biome. The bundled map JSON (~43 kB) is still in the entry: maps/registry.ts is read synchronously by MapSystem, routing, the StartMenu and the persistence layer. Raised 709,000 -> 722,000 B (#486 B-D, gamepad / touch / comfort): main was already at 711,846 B once the duplicate RunResultsPanel import in GameHUD (a bad merge that stops the bundle building at all) is removed, +2.8 kB over this ceiling; this PR adds 9.3 kB to that (721,170 B). It would have been ~19 kB: GamepadSource + gamepad mapping (4.3 kB), the haptics envelopes (1.5 kB), the menu-focus engine (3.6 kB), the debug hotkeys (0.9 kB) and the handheld envelope (1.3 kB) are all dynamic imports now (gamepadconnected / first menu / ?debug=1 / touch device), as are the touch layer and source. What stays in the entry is the part every player runs: the settings store v2 (+2.4 kB, 11 comfort / haptics / gamepad / touch fields + the v1 -> v2 migration), the comfort resolver and its live cache (+1.1 kB), the PAUSE bus and edge, the look-apply component, InputHubTick's pad loader, and the thin lazy facades. Raised 722,000 -> 734,000 B (#464 A-F, the living river): main is at 711,860 B; this adds 21.4 kB (733,214 B). New modules, raw: the WeatherDirector + weather script + its tick and reach fraction (4.5 kB), the sky clock + NOAA sun position + map atmosphere + its tick (3.1 kB), the erosion integrator + plane codec + live field (~4.5 kB), the squall front (0.9 kB), the xoshiro PRNG + FNV hash (1.1 kB), the SWE checksum (0.3 kB); the rest is growth in modules already there (router lateral/weather plumbing, run conditions, the water-sheet lookup, sweHost's clock). All of it runs every frame of every run, so it rides the boot path like the hub. Kept off it: Today's River card + generator (StartMenu, lazy), the replay plan loader (?replay= only), ScriptedSource. Raised 734,000 -> 738,000 B (raft + player rivers, phases A/C/F): main is at 733,327 B; this adds 4.1 kB (737,421 B). In the entry, because every run reads it: the vehicle water datum the raft's floating check and OOB share with the force bridge, the raft envelope, the StartMenu vehicle picker and its map-scoped choice, and the user-river session (getRunMap / the run key / ghost fairness resolve through it). Kept off it: the .wsriver import + saved-river list (UserRiverPanel, lazy, with the level validator) and the editor's ?river= hand-off loader. Lowered 738,000 -> 736,000 B (#503 E/F, layering + tests on top of the #512 code-health pass): main 737,421 -> 735,907 B — the window boundary events and RunnerVehicle/utils went, the rest are moves that do not change the entry. Raised 736,000 -> 737,000 B (#518 B, gameplay on sim time): main 735,907 -> 736,956 B (+1.0 kB). The biome cross-fade's sim-time clock (advanceBiomeTransition) and memoised provider, the ChunkManager debounce counted in update(dt) plus the spawn-biome report, the SWE readiness state the scripted harness waits on, and src/utils/wallClock.ts. All of it runs on every frame of every run, so it stays on the boot path. Raised 737,000 -> 741,000 B (#521 A, SimCore): main 736,100 -> 740,019 B (+3.9 kB). New on the boot path, all of it runs every frame of every run: SimCore itself (fixed-step accumulator, ordered registry, SimContext and its run stream), SimCoreTick (the −90 sample of camera / vehicle / hub frame into the context), and the system adapters that were already in the entry as frame callbacks and are now registry entries (weather, sky, chunk biome, survival, pillar clocks, score + ghost clock) plus their composition list. Nothing left the entry in exchange: the callbacks they replace were bodies inside components that stay. Rounded up to the next kB. Lowered 741,000 -> 738,000 B (#521 B-F): main 740,020 -> 737,815 B (-2.2 kB). On the boot path and new: the GameplayProfile table + its sim system, the biome store (zustand vanilla) and selector hooks, queryFlags, the runner step's scratch and stages. Off it, behind their flags: App's dev toggles / overlays / replay-river autostart / editor (harness/), the ?screenshot=1 harness API (harness/screenshotApi.ts, 2.1 kB), the F3 movement panel (MovementReadoutPanel, 3 kB); and knip's dead code is gone. Rounded up to the next kB. Raised 738,000 -> 740,000 B (#522 A, the hazard skeleton): main 737,881 -> 739,782 B (+1.9 kB). The hazards themselves are lazy per map (the issue's payload rule): the runtime (lifecycle, parser, anchors, the hazard log) is its own hazardRuntime chunk (4 kB), fetched only by a run whose map authors hazards[]. What stays on the boot path runs or is read on every run: SimCore's `hazards` facade (one hazards[] lookup per step), ctx.water (launch hour, the parsed hydroEvents cache, the SWE stage probe the host names each frame), the survival shock a hit applies, and the persistence / .wsghost guards for the v5 hazards[] log (a stored rival is checked on every load). Rounded up to the next kB. Raised 740,000 -> 741,000 B (#487 D, placement on the tile): main 739,782 -> 740,776 B (+1.0 kB). terrain/placement.ts (the sampler-driven port of all 31 categories into one packed buffer) replaces populateZSteps / populateSidePart1/2 on the boot path — the boot and restart pools build their placements synchronously, so the builder cannot be lazy — and the adapter that materialises the object lists, plus sampleTile / buildWallShellTile in terrainTile.ts. The port is close to the size of what it replaced; the +1 kB is the packed-buffer header / reader and the sampler. Rounded up to the next kB. Raised 741,000 -> 747,000 B (#466 audit A-D, rendering + delivery): main was already at 742,503 B (1.5 kB over, after #533), this adds 3.8 kB (746,308 B). On the boot path because they run every frame or at Canvas mount: the whole-frame renderer.info snapshot (frameRenderInfo), the AA-tier latch, rock-texture anisotropy, the Rapier proxy's failure kinds + INIT deadline + protocol check, and the ShaderWarmup host (its menu trigger, the warm-frame useFrame and the first-3-s program count). Kept off it: the warm-up itself (core + recipes + the factories they call + the warm-frame composer setup, shaderWarmupRun chunk, 6.3 kB, fetched while the menu is up) and drei's Stats (DebugStats chunk, ?debug=1 only). Rounded up to the next kB. Lowered 747,000 -> 738,000 B (#554 A.1 + D): main 742,172 -> 737,273 B. WaterFlowForces (the segment-spline raft current that never ran) and WATER_FLOW_CONFIG are deleted (-4.9 kB); the rest is headroom main was already carrying (742,172 against 747,000). The dependency bumps moved nothing in the entry (React, R3F and drei land in vendor-three). Rounded up to the next kB. Raised 738,000 -> 739,000 B (#554 E, B.1, B.4): 737,273 -> 738,301 B. E +136 B (the pool snapshot state in TrackManager, getRunMapId / resolveRunMap, the latest-value refs), B.1 +467 B (halfFloatPack: the 512-entry base / shift table build and the bulk packer, on the boot path because the SWE upload runs every step), B.4 +425 B (startNativeWasmPrefetch / takeNativeWasmBytes and the INIT handover). C moved nothing in the entry. Rounded up to the next kB. Raised 739,000 -> 740,000 B (#556 A, gameplay out of React): main 737,652 -> 739,428 B (+1.8 kB). On the boot path because every run steps them: the runner step as a SimCore system (runnerSimSystem) and the Rapier world's step as another (rapierWorldSimSystem + RapierSimStep), the run-state port (simGame: SimGameView, the plain view a fresh core holds, the store binding), the vehicle cue events and the runner's cue subscriber (sounds / shake / bursts were inline calls), the camera follow as field writes and the FOV kick out of the step, launchRewards (moved out of LaunchScoringSession, not new) and the copy-on-write listener lists that replace the bus's EventTarget. The raft's cue subscriber rides the lazy RaftVehicle chunk. Rounded up to the next kB. Raised 740,000 -> 742,000 B (River Workshop A + D): main 739,428 -> 741,122 B (+1.7 kB). The Workshop itself is a lazy chunk (workshopMaxBytes below); what stays on the boot path is what reaches it and what a shared river needs on every run: the StartMenu's RIVER WORKSHOP button and its chunk preload, MenuShell's lazy host and loading fallback, useGamePhase's workshop phase (open / close, the Test-run start and the return to the Workshop when that run ends, Enter-to-start held while it is open), the Your Rivers panel's Open-in-Workshop prop, queryFlags' currentHash, and canonicalJson (+0.9 kB of source), which hashUserRiverLevel now hashes so a river's key is the same from a file, an export or a shared link (the ghost fairness key, D.3). The link codec and fflate are not on it: riverShare.ts rides the lazy userRiverImport chunk. Rounded up to the next kB. Raised 742,000 -> 757,000 B (#566, typed i18n — misses the issue's <= 4 kB target; see the PR): main 741,194 -> 756,709 B (+15.5 kB). ~9.3 kB of it is the message keys themselves: 481 key literals (254 distinct, ~25 B each) sit in the boot catalog and again at every t() call site, and a minifier cannot shorten a string. The rest (~6.2 kB) is the runtime (t() with cached template parts and PluralRules, the Intl formatter cache, useT, resolveLocale, registerEnglish), the settings store's v3 locale field, SettingsSync's locale apply, the HUD's air-time writer and per-locale readout formatters, and messages that are new (aria-labels the screens lacked). Kept off it: es / fr (lazy chunks, ~21 kB each) and the English of every lazy screen (Options, pause, results, touch, Today's River, Your Rivers ride their own chunks via registerEnglish, -7 kB from the entry). Getting under +4 kB needs keys gone from the bundle: a build step that rewrites keys to short ids (~-7.5 kB) or Paraglide's compiled message functions (#566's named fallback); both leave ~+8 kB, so the choice is the owner's. Rounded up to the next kB. Raised 757,000 -> 758,000 B (#556 A.1 + B.1): main 756,709 -> 757,017 B (+0.3 kB). Both on the boot path because every frame of every run takes them: A.1's SimContext debug sink (the runner step's snapshot goes out through ctx.debug instead of importing the harness taps: +~150 B for the sink, its silent default and the browser binding), and the shared sample (experience/simContextSample.ts: what SimCoreTick reads of the world into SimCore moved out unchanged so the headless harness fills the same context with the same function, +~170 B for the call and its argument object). The headless harness itself (src/sim/headless/) is in no chunk: Node-only, imported by tests alone (scripts/check-dependency-direction.mjs). Rounded up to the next kB. Raised 758,000 -> 765,000 B (#558 B-D, access): main 757,017 -> 764,266 B (+7.2 kB). On the boot path because every frame or every run reads it: the settings store's v4 fields and their migration (UI scale, colour vision, captions, the assists, hold / toggle), SettingsSync's apply of the UI scale, the palette custom properties and the store-free accessRuntime (live assists, the sticky run bits, the hold modes), the authored palette + grade / glyph tables (access.ts), the HUD bars' shape-and-word state and the ASSISTED badge (GameHUD +1.1 kB, hud.ts +0.3 kB), the ghost split's glyph + word, hold / toggle in the input hub (holdToggle.ts, 0.75 kB), the non-lethal clamp (runSession), game speed in SimCoreTick / the raft / the water forces, the auto-jump check (autoJump.ts, 0.45 kB) and the gap t on segment frames, and the assists in the run key, .wsghost and fairness verdict. ForecastHUD's inline styles moved to access.css (-0.6 kB). Kept off it: the caption layer, its router and its English (CaptionLayer chunk, fetched when captions are on), the colour-vision palettes (palettes chunk, fetched for a mode other than Default), the guide ribbon (GuideRibbon chunk, mounted only with the assist on) and the Accessibility / Assist pages' English (SettingsPanel chunk). Rounded up to the next kB.

It also loads the shared userRiverImport (validator glue, fflate, riverShare) and levelValidator chunks the StartMenu's river panel already uses. Rounded up to the next kB; phases B / C (schema-driven inspector, hazards palette, timeline, live SWE) raise it with their own reasons.
